title: 🏛️ Exams 2007–2023 · pronouns in exam texts: object, reflexive, possessive ⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2013, technical) Jim is a painter, and it is his birthday tomorrow. Complete the sentence: "His wife is going to buy ___ a lovely present."
questions.explanation: The gap follows the verb buy and names the person who receives the present, so the pronoun takes its object form: him. He is the subject form, his needs a noun after it, and himself could only point back to a man who is the subject, but the subject here is his wife.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2012, technical) A parent writes about a teenage daughter and the Internet: "She talks about school life with her friends and shares songs with ___."
questions.explanation: The pronoun follows the preposition with and stands for the friends, several people, so it takes the object form: them. They is the subject form, her would mean one other girl, and themselves points back to a subject that is not the daughter.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2007) Two parents write to an adviser about their son Richard, who stays out very late at night. Complete the sentence: "In fact, we are only concerned about ___ future."
questions.explanation: The gap comes right before the noun future and tells whose future it is, so it needs the possessive form: his future. Him is the object form, he is the subject form, and himself is a reflexive pronoun, which never stands before a noun.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2023, technical) A text about the colour green says: "Plants are green, and without ___ the earth wouldn't be such a lovely home for us."
questions.explanation: The pronoun follows the preposition without and replaces plants, which is plural, so it takes the object form: them. Him and her each stand for one person, and they is the subject form.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021, technical) A woman talks about her work as a car mechanic. She says: "That job made ___ a much stronger person today."
questions.explanation: The woman is speaking about herself, so the person who became stronger is the speaker, I, and after the verb made the pronoun takes its object form: me. It and them stand for things or for several people, and her would be another woman.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2018, technical) A father of two girls and one boy worries about his children's pastime. Complete the sentence: "All of ___ have access to the internet."
questions.explanation: After the preposition of, the pronoun takes its object form, and here it stands for the three children: all of them. They is the subject form, their needs a noun after it, and him is one boy only.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2018, technical) A couple tell how they built the house where they now live. Complete the sentence: "Building our ___ house was a dream that we achieved."
questions.explanation: Own stands between a possessive adjective and a noun to stress that the thing belongs to its owner and nobody else: our own house. One counts things, and self is only the end of a reflexive pronoun (ourselves), never a word placed before a noun.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2010, general) A teenager writes about her working mother: "I have always thought everyone lived like ___, but now that I am at secondary school, I realize that there are mothers who don't work at all."
questions.explanation: After the preposition like, the pronoun takes its object form: like me. My needs a noun after it, mine replaces a noun that belongs to the speaker, and I is the subject form, which cannot follow a preposition.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2015, general) Daisy's father moved his family all over the country. When his wife asked him to stay in one place, he would laugh and ask "Why?" Complete the next sentence: "Then he would answer ___ 'Girls don't need an education.'"
questions.explanation: The one who asks the question and the one who answers it are the same person, the father, so the object is the reflexive pronoun for he: himself. Myself is for I, herself is for a woman, and the plain object form him would mean another man.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021, general) A text about cycling says: "Even if you don't have a car, a bike can pay for ___ when compared to the price of bus tickets."
questions.explanation: The subject is a bike, a thing, and it is also the one that pays: the object is the same as the subject, so the reflexive pronoun for it is needed: itself. Yourself, herself and themselves each point back to another subject.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2019, general) A text about volunteering says that it means helping people who may not be able to help ___.
questions.explanation: The people who need help are the same people who cannot do the helping, so the reflexive pronoun for they is needed: themselves. Yourself and yourselves stand for you, and himself stands for one man.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2009, technical) A worker describes his morning: "Before I start my job, I put on my uniform and look at ___ in the mirror."
questions.explanation: The one who looks and the one who is seen are the same person, and the subject is I, so the object becomes the reflexive pronoun for I: myself. The object form me does not point back to the subject, and yourself and himself are for other people.
